kept.claim: Backup-code consumption is an unguarded read-decrypt-modify-write with no transaction or optimistic check, so concurrent logins with the same code can all succeed, which breaks the single-use guarantee.
kept.body:
## [RACE CONDITION] A backup code can be used more than once by sending requests in parallel

**Severity:** MEDIUM — breaks the "each backup code can be used exactly once" promise (`backup_code_instructions`).

### The Problem

```ts
const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({ ... select: { backupCodes: true, ... } }); // read
...
const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, KEY));
const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));
if (index === -1) throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode);
backupCodes[index] = null;                                   // line 148
await prisma.user.update({ where: { id: user.id }, data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) } }); // blind write
```

The `update` filters only on `id`, not on the ciphertext that was read. Take N concurrent requests with the same code. All of them read the same `backupCodes` blob before any write lands, all find the code, all null out the same index, and all write. Each one returns a session.

The same read-modify-write also loses updates when two *different* codes are used at once. Request A writes `[null, c1, ...]`, then request B writes `[c0, null, ...]`, so code 0 becomes usable again.

### Theory / Proof

This is a classic TOCTOU / lost-update. Prisma's `update` with `where: { id }` does no compare-and-set, and there is no `$transaction` or row lock around the read. The rate limiter (`checkRateLimitAndThrowError`, `Ratelimit.fixedWindow(10, "60s")` in `packages/lib/rateLimit.ts`) still allows 10 requests per window, and it is a no-op returning `remaining: 999` when Upstash env vars are absent (self-hosted default).

### What happens today vs. what will break

A single user logging in sequentially works fine. An attacker who has intercepted one code, or a user whose code sits in a shared file, can mint several sessions in parallel from one "single-use" code. The lost-update case quietly brings a spent code back to life.

### Research

OWASP ASVS V2.6.1 requires that "lookup secrets can be used only once". Common implementations such as django-otp `StaticToken` delete the row atomically, or do a conditional update on the previous value.

### Recommendation

Make the write conditional on the value that was read, and fail if nothing was updated:

```ts
backupCodes[index] = null;
const { count } = await prisma.user.updateMany({
  where: { id: user.id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }, // compare-and-set
  data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) },
});
if (count === 0) throw new Error(ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode);
```
kept.evidence: next-auth-options.ts:73-102 does a plain findUnique; bcrypt runs at 125-128, then lines 146-153 update where {id} with no compare-and-set. The rate limiter allows 10 requests per 60s (rateLimit.ts:58) and is a no-op without Upstash (rateLimit.ts:45-49). The attack also needs the password, because the password check at 121-129 runs first.

kept.claim: 2FA is already enabled on the server before the backup-codes step, but dismissing the dialog with Esc or an outside click at that step calls only onOpenChange, not onEnable. The settings switch then stays 'disabled', and reopening the modal shows the stale backup-codes step.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step leaves the UI out of sync with the server

**Severity:** MEDIUM — the user sees 2FA as disabled when it is actually enabled.

### The Problem

`handleEnable` now moves to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` after `/totp/enable` returns 200, instead of calling `onEnable()`. At that point `twoFactorEnabled` is already `true` in the DB. `onEnable()` (which runs `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()` in `pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx`) is only called from the **Close** button:

```tsx
<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>   // line 166
...
<Button data-testid="backup-codes-close" onClick={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); resetState(); onEnable(); }}>
```

Radix `Dialog` fires `onOpenChange(false)` on Escape and on an outside pointer-down. The parent wires that to `setEnableModalOpen(!enableModalOpen)`. That closes the modal but does not invalidate `viewer.me`, and `resetState()` is not called.

### What happens today vs. what will break

1. The user enables 2FA and reaches the backup-codes step.
2. The user presses Esc, which is natural after downloading the codes.
3. The switch and badge still say "Disabled", because the `viewer.me` query is stale.
4. Clicking the switch again calls `setEnableModalOpen(true)`, since the page thinks 2FA is off. `step` is still `DisplayBackupCodes` (the component stays mounted and was never reset), so the old codes reappear. The UI only corrects itself after a refetch or a full page reload.

The old flow did not have this gap, because `onEnable()` ran as soon as the server confirmed.

### Research

Radix Dialog docs: `onOpenChange` is called on Escape key down and on interact-outside unless those events are prevented (`onEscapeKeyDown` / `onPointerDownOutside`).

### Recommendation

Treat any close on the backup-codes step as completion:

```tsx
<Dialog
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={(isOpen) => {
    if (!isOpen && step === SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes) {
      resetState();
      onEnable();
      return;
    }
    onOpenChange();
  }}>
```

Also clear `backupCodes` and revoke `backupCodesUrl` in `resetState()`, so the plaintext codes and the Blob URL do not stay in memory.
kept.evidence: EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:134-136 sets the step instead of calling onEnable. The @calcom/ui Dialog/DialogContent (packages/ui/components/dialog/Dialog.tsx:27-126) does not block Escape or outside clicks. two-factor-auth.tsx:64 onOpenChange only toggles the modal and never invalidates viewer.me. The stale step reappears on reopen. The 'refresh then TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled' sub-claim was wrong and has been removed.

kept.claim: Users who enabled 2FA before this PR have backupCodes = null and there is no way to generate or regenerate codes without disabling 2FA, yet the 'Lost access' button is shown to them and the error text tells them to 'generate them in your settings', which is not possible.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] No way to generate or regenerate backup codes for existing 2FA users

**Severity:** LOW — a misleading recovery path for every existing 2FA user, and no replenishment once the 10 codes are used up.

### The Problem

Backup codes are only created in `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, which returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` when `user.twoFactorEnabled` is true. The migration adds a nullable column with no backfill:

```sql
ALTER TABLE "users" ADD COLUMN "backupCodes" TEXT;
```

So every user who enabled 2FA before this deploy gets:

```ts
if (!user.backupCodes) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes);   // line 137
```

The login page still shows the "Lost access" button to them. The resulting message (`missing_backup_codes` in `common.json`) says *"No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings."*, but no settings UI or API generates them. The same happens once a user has spent all 10 codes (they become `null` entries and are never refilled), except then the error is `IncorrectBackupCode`.

### What happens today vs. what will break

New 2FA setups work. Existing users locked out of their authenticator follow the "Lost access" flow and hit a dead end whose message points them to a feature that does not exist.

### Research

GitHub, Google and GitLab all provide a "regenerate recovery codes" action, gated behind password and 2FA re-verification, and warn when few codes remain.

### Recommendation

Either add a regenerate endpoint (a `POST /api/auth/two-factor/totp/backup-codes` that verifies password + TOTP, generates 10 new codes and returns them), or at least correct the copy:

```json
"missing_backup_codes": "No backup codes found. Disable and re-enable two-factor authentication in your settings to generate them."
```
kept.evidence: setup.ts:42-44 refuses setup when 2FA is already enabled. The migration does not backfill existing users. No route regenerates codes. The 'Lost access' button is always shown, and missing_backup_codes tells users to generate codes in settings, which is not possible.
